answer: Only 40% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. Because the bridge ledger attributes every share, the tide audit publishes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it forfeits the terrace fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 36 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
